name: worktree-write-scope-decisions
body:
Worktree-only write scope for code-writer agents deepens `requirements.constraint.code-writer-scope-worktree-only`. Model: every generated code-writer agent's `edit` grants target the worktree mirror `apg/.worktrees/*/` rather than a repo-root path. opencode resolves path-scoped globs against the session workspace root (the main checkout), so the worktree form reaches the worktree, and a root grant makes main writable. fs scope resolution: the fs tools resolve the candidate path to an absolute path against the session workspace root (the main-checkout root opencode uses) and assert the `edit` action with that resolved path as the resource, so opencode's permission engine applies the acting agent's effective `edit` scope (allow and deny, last match wins) in one frame, and an absolute path outside `
/apg/.worktrees/

/` is refused. The acting agent's identity and the per-path decision follow the mechanism `requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission` states, and `external_directory` governs an out-of-worktree path. An unresolvable acting agent refuses every path. Release-agent: releases run from MAIN, so the release-agent's write grants target the main checkout; it is one of the two agent carve-outs of `global.constraint.worktree-isolation` and carries zero worktree mirror. Its main-write set is repo-specific: the agent-builder analyses the repo (version files, packaging formulae, changelog, release scripts) and recommends the set, confirmed through the coordinator interview like build gates and test tiers; the spec fixes the policy alone.
